title: Zooplankton
author: Wikipedia contributors
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, “Zooplankton”, English Wikipedia. Text available under CC BY-SA 4.0; see source history for contributors.
paragraphs: Zooplankton are the heterotrophic component of the planktonic community, having to consume other organisms to thrive. The name comes from Ancient Greek ζῷον (zōîon), meaning "animal", and πλαγκτός (planktós), meaning "drifter, wanderer, roamer", and thus, "animal drifter". Plankton are aquatic organisms that are unable to swim effectively against currents. Consequently, they drift or are carried along by currents in the ocean, or by currents in seas, lakes or rivers.

Zooplankton can be contrasted with phytoplankton (cyanobacteria and microalgae), which are the plant-like component of the plankton community (the "phyto-" prefix comes from Ancient Greek: φῠτόν, romanized: phutón, lit. 'plant', although taxonomically not plants). Zooplankton are heterotrophic (other-feeding), whereas phytoplankton are autotrophic (self-feeding), often generating biological energy and macromolecules through chlorophyllic carbon fixation using sunlight – in other words, zooplankton cannot manufacture their own food, while phytoplankton can. As a result, zooplankton must acquire nutrients by feeding on other organisms such as phytoplankton, which are generally smaller than zooplankton. Most zooplankton are microscopic but some (such as jellyfish) are macroscopic, meaning they can be seen with the naked eye.

Many protozoans (single-celled protists that prey on other microscopic life) are zooplankton, including zooflagellates, foraminiferans, radiolarians, some dinoflagellates and marine microanimals. Macroscopic zooplankton include pelagic cnidarians, ctenophores, molluscs, arthropods and tunicates, as well as planktonic arrow worms and bristle worms.

The distinction between autotrophy and heterotrophy often breaks down in very small organisms. Recent studies of marine microplankton have indicated over half of microscopic plankton are mixotrophs, which can obtain energy and carbon from a mix of internal plastids and external sources. Many marine microzooplankton are mixotrophic, which means they could also be classified as phytoplankton.

sentence.text: Most zooplankton are microscopic but some (such as jellyfish) are macroscopic, meaning they can be seen with the naked eye.
sentence.translation: 大多数浮游动物非常微小，需要借助显微镜观察，但有些，例如水母，体型较大，肉眼就能看见。
sentence.analysis: but 连接两个形成对比的并列分句：Most zooplankton are microscopic 和 some ... are macroscopic。some 代指 some zooplankton，避免重复；括号中的 such as jellyfish 是举例说明。meaning 引出的现在分词短语补充解释 macroscopic 的含义，后接省略 that 的内容从句 they can be seen with the naked eye。can be seen 是“情态动词 + be + 过去分词”的被动结构，表示“能够被看见”；with the naked eye 表示观察所用的方式。

questions.prompt: 根据第一段，浮游生物为什么主要随水流漂移？
options: 它们只在水面结冰时移动
它们必须依靠风直接推动身体
它们不能有效地逆着水流游动
它们都生活在没有水流的封闭水域中
questions.explanation: 第一段说明浮游生物 unable to swim effectively against currents，随后以 Consequently 引出结果：它们漂移或被水流携带。因此关键是逆流游动能力不足，而不是完全不会移动。
hints: 区分原因与结果，不要把相关现象直接当作因果。
回到第 1 段，逐项核对主体、范围及表示条件或程度的词。

questions.prompt: 最后一段对前文的异养与自养区分作了什么补充？
options: 只有肉眼可见的生物才可能采用混合营养方式
所有浮游动物都能够完全依靠阳光生活
浮游植物和浮游动物之间不存在任何差别
一些微小生物兼有两种营养方式，因此分类边界并不总是清晰
questions.explanation: 最后一段指出这种区分在很小的生物中常常不成立，并介绍 mixotrophs。许多海洋微型浮游动物可同时利用内部质体和外部来源，所以也可能被归为浮游植物。
hints: 先看例子或连接词前后的观点，再判断它的作用。
回到第 4 段，逐项核对主体、范围及表示条件或程度的词。
